learningObjective: The count for the next step is the sum of the counts for the two preceding positions.

mechanismReview.pattern: One-dimensional dynamic programming compressed to the last two answers.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: The task counts paths to position n, every final move has one of two fixed lengths, and paths ending with different final moves are disjoint.
mechanismReview.invariant: Before each iteration, previous and current are consecutive recurrence values. Parallel assignment shifts current into previous and stores previous + current as the complete count for the next step.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Only two integers are needed because ways(i) depends solely on ways(i - 1) and ways(i - 2). The loop index identifies which stair count current represents.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: An indexed stair sequence shows fill order and both predecessor dependencies, while stable previous/current keys visibly advance one position per update and printed equations preserve meaning without animation.
rejectedAlternatives: A full binary recursion tree repeats the same subproblems and obscures the linear recurrence.
A complete DP table stores more history than the implementation needs.
A Fibonacci label alone requires memorizing the recurrence rather than seeing why the two predecessor counts add.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: Classify solutions by their final decision: if every state can only arrive from a fixed small set of predecessor states, add those disjoint counts and retain only the dependency horizon.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.
